chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥarīz, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who inflicted a muḍiḥah wound upon a slave, he said: “Upon him is one-half of one-tenth of the slave’s value, payable to the slave’s master, and the slave’s price is not to exceed the blood-money of a free person.”

key_terms.دِيَةَ الْحُرِّ: the blood-money of a free person
key_terms.شَجَّ: inflicted a head or facial wound
key_terms.قِيمَةِ الْعَبْدِ: the monetary value of the slave used as the basis for compensation
key_terms.مُوضِحَةً: a wound that exposes the bone
key_terms.نِصْفُ عُشْرِ: half of one-tenth, namely a fixed fractional amount

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for inflicting a muḍiḥah wound on a slave in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for compensation when a slave suffers a muḍiḥah wound. It states that the compensation is a fixed proportion of the slave’s value, paid to the master, while also setting an upper limit so that the slave’s valuation does not exceed the diyah of a free person.
